Lola Young has announced the Everything Begins Tour, a 17-date North American headline run set for spring 2027. It will be her first sustained tour of the region since she stepped away from live work in 2025, after a period in which her return happened gradually through individual performances and festivals rather than another long itinerary. The new run follows a year spent rebuilding her live schedule without immediately replacing the tour she had cancelled.

The break began after Young collapsed during her set at All Things Go in New York and then cancelled her remaining performances for the foreseeable future. She said she needed time to work on herself and asked listeners to give her "a second chance" when she was ready to return. There was no comeback date attached to that message. When performances resumed, they came one at a time, which made the process feel less like a relaunch and more like a deliberate test of how much live work she actually wanted to take on again.

At the Grammys, "Messy" won Best Pop Solo Performance. She performed the song during the ceremony in one of her first major appearances after the break. Headline shows in Britain and festival sets followed through the year, including a return to All Things Go. By the time Everything Begins was announced, she had already spent months performing again, but she had not committed to another extended North American run until now.

[apple:song:6768357139:6768357142]

"From Down Here" arrived during that rebuilding period and gave the return new material instead of leaving it attached only to the album cycle that had been interrupted. Young has said inspiration hit the day after the Grammys and that she went into the studio with James Blake to make the song. She described it as coming from the uneasy position of missing an old high while knowing that a more grounded life is safer and more rewarding. The track is calmer than much of *I'm Only F**king Myself* without sanding away the bluntness that made "Messy" connect so widely.

The tour title comes from Young's "Everything Ends" tattoo, reversing a phrase that was already part of her before the cancellations. The wording could easily have been turned into a comeback slogan, but the sequence of events makes it more specific than that. She did not disappear and then announce a tour as proof that everything had changed. She returned to individual stages, released new music, kept testing the shape of live work and only then committed to a 17-show North American run. Everything Begins is the first time that gradual return has become a fixed multiweek plan rather than another isolated appearance.
